headline: Rate-hike odds and a chip pullback muddy a risk-on tape
body: Futures point modestly higher into Tuesday's open -- S&P 500 futures up roughly 0.1% and the Nasdaq 100 closer to 0.4% -- but the tape is doing more digesting than celebrating. Long-end Treasury yields have pushed to multi-year highs (the 10-year near 4.71%, the 30-year at levels not seen in nearly two decades), and with new Fed leadership under Kevin Warsh, futures markets are pricing meaningful odds of a September rate hike rather than the cuts investors spent much of the year expecting. That repricing has hit semiconductors hardest: Intel, AMD and Taiwan Semiconductor have all shed several percent into Nvidia's Wednesday earnings, as investors question whether AI-spending growth still justifies current multiples. Fresh U.S. sanctions on Iran add a geopolitical layer, though markets have so far treated it as background noise rather than a risk-off trigger.

Under the surface, the mood reads as risk-on but thinning -- the VIX spent much of August near 2026 lows on light hedging and heavy call buying, a classic complacency signal that has begun creaking as chip stocks wobble and yields climb into the historically rockier September-October stretch. Retail chatter isn't adding much new texture today: trackers show Nvidia, Google and SpaceX topping WallStreetBets mention counts with a bullish tilt, alongside a resurgence in GameStop mentions, but nothing that reads as a distinct catalyst -- this read leans more on price action, rates and the chip-sector pullback than on social sentiment. Overall, it looks like a market pausing to reprice rate expectations rather than one turning genuinely defensive.
